title: The four authorise operations have no request, response or error schema in any source
source: 02 Business architecture and process/Recovery Workbench Users Roles and Permissions v4.xlsx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet; new sheet Authorise contract, table A1
description: Architecture v5 names four rwb-access operations as the access contract every service uses (POST /authorise with role, scope and DoA; GET /me/permissions; GET /doa-limits; GET /masking-policies), but no source in this work pack gives an operation ID, a request or response body, a status code or an error model for them. The Endpoints sheet of the Ownership Map lists only the four P4 administration operations carried from API Specification v4.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14, P4 IN: 'REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA) · GET /me/permissions · GET /doa-limits · /masking-policies'; slide 41 row P4 first API path /authorise; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet: GET /admin/roles, GET /admin/access-log, GET /me/session, POST /admin/break-glass-grants, all x-module P4.
proposed: The P4 contract story RWB-P4-E1037-CON publishes the OpenAPI document with the operation IDs, bodies, status codes and error model from the operation names Architecture v5 gives; v5 cites the three inputs the slide names and marks the body as a placeholder until then.

title: The sign-in permission read has two names, /me/permissions and /me/session
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet; Authorise contract table A1
description: Architecture v5 gives rwb-access GET /me/permissions. The API Specification v4 operation that the Ownership Map records for P4 is GET /me/session. Both read the signed-in user's roles and neither source says whether they are one operation under two names or two operations.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14, P4 IN: 'GET /me/permissions'; slide 41; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet row 'GET /me/session' with basis 'API Specification v4 (same x-module since v2), x-module P4'.
proposed: /me/permissions is carried as the contract name because Template and Rules R3 puts Architecture v5 above the story masters; the P4 contract story maps /me/session to it and records the rename in the API catalogue.

title: No cache lifetime and no rule for a failed authorise call
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
section: Architecture v5 slide 35; Authorise contract A9 step 3 and A10
description: Architecture v5 says each service authorises the object itself using cached permission data from rwb-access, with a 2 s timeout and a circuit breaker, but no source in this pack states how long the cache lives, how it is refreshed beyond the two access events, or whether a service allows or refuses an action when rwb-access does not answer.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 35: 'Each service authorises the object itself (OWASP API1 object-level authorisation), using cached permission data from rwb-access. Timeouts 2 s, circuit breaker per downstream, GET retry once with jitter'; slide 43 additions row: AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged, consumers 'all (cache refresh)'; no lifetime and no failure rule in any source read for this work pack.
proposed: The P4 contract story fixes the cache lifetime and the failure rule; v5 records the fail-closed reading, the refresh on AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged, and the 5 minute membership refresh the access story already assumes under DL38; the lifetime stays a placeholder.

title: The DoA limit amounts are not in this document
source: 02 Business architecture and process/Recovery Workbench Users Roles and Permissions v4.xlsx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: Permissions tab note row; Key tab 'A' row; Authorise contract A6 delegation_limit
description: Every approve letter of the Permissions tab works within the delegation of authority table, but no amount, loss percentage, product or approver level is stated in this workbook. The table is owned by P4 per the Ownership Map, and the DoA rule versions appear only in the Temporal and Drools design.
evidence: Permissions tab row 2: 'Every approve right works within the delegation of authority table'; Key tab row 'A'; Ownership Map v1 Tables: delegation_limit owner P4; Temporal and Drools design: 'Rule version DOA-2026.11', 'DOA-2027.01'.
proposed: v5 names the owner (P4), the table (delegation_limit) and the two operations that serve it; the amounts stay in the Delegation of Authority Matrix and the DoA rule package and no amount is copied into this document.

title: The masking rules per role, area and field group are not in this document
source: 02 Business architecture and process/Recovery Workbench Users Roles and Permissions v4.xlsx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: Permissions tab; Access flow tab; Authorise contract A1 /masking-policies and A6 masking_rule
description: The workbook says personal data is masked and the Ownership Map gives P4 a masking_rule table, but the workbook does not state which role sees which field group in clear, the mask shape or the field list. The access story puts the masking values with Compliance under DL26 and no source in this pack gives them.
evidence: Access flow tab, Joiner step 5: 'Resolves the roles, scope and masking'; Ownership Map v1 Tables: masking_rule owner P4; access story RWB-E1-037 precondition 'MASK-2026.11 is loaded ... DL26' and BR6.
proposed: v5 names P4 as owner of masking_rule and GET /masking-policies as the contract; the rule values stay with Compliance and are loaded as a versioned reference data set.

title: Partner roles sit in the roles table while the partner user is owned by S9
source: 02 Business architecture and process/Recovery Workbench Users Roles and Permissions v4.xlsx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: Roles tab PT rows; Ownership Map v1 Rulings sheet (partner_user); Authorise contract A11
description: The workbook holds seven partner roles as role rows like any other role. The Ownership Map splits them: partner_user is owned by S9 rwb-partner and P4 keeps only the internal role model. No source says how a partner user resolves to a partner role code or which service holds that link.
evidence: Roles tab: PT-AGENCY, PT-LAWFIRM, PT-VALUER, PT-AUCTION, PT-BUYER, PT-RAMC, PT-LED; Ownership Map v1 Tables: partner_user owner S9 with ruling 'Partner users stay with S9 rwb-partner ... P4 keeps the internal role model only'; Architecture v5 slide 41, S9 owns partner users.
proposed: The PT role rows, their letters and their default scope stay with P4; the partner user record, the instruction and the result stay with S9; S9 asks POST /authorise with the PT role code and holds the user-to-role link.

title: The access log is named by Architecture v5 but is not itemised in the Ownership Map
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet; Authorise contract A1 and A6
description: Architecture v5 puts an access log in the rwb_access schema and gives the administration operation GET /admin/access-log, but the Ownership Map Tables sheet has no access log row, so the table name, its columns, its retention and its hash rule are not stated anywhere in this pack.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14, P4 DB line: 'schema rwb_access: Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, DoA table, access log'; slide 41; Ownership Map v1 Tables: role, permission, role_conflict, masking_rule, delegation_limit for P4, and no access log row.
proposed: The access log is read as a P4 table in rwb_access, append-only and created by the P4 DB story RWB-P4-E1039-DB; v5 names the owner and the read operation and leaves the definition to that story and to the Ownership Map.

title: How the six non-human actors authenticate is not stated
source: 02 Business architecture and process/Recovery Workbench Users Roles and Permissions v4.xlsx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
section: Roles tab SY rows; Permissions tab SY rows; Authorise contract A11
description: The six non-human actors hold permission rows like a bank role, but no source says how a managed identity authenticates to rwb-access, whether it calls POST /authorise or relies on mTLS alone, or whether its rows are checked at sign-in.
evidence: Roles tab: SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-RECOVERY, SY-OCR, SY-DECLOG, SY-AGENT; Single sign-on tab gives each a managed identity group per environment; Architecture v5 slide 35: 'Every call encrypted and identified both ways (mTLS)'.
proposed: The six actors are resolved through the same POST /authorise path with their SY role code and their managed identity as the subject; the credential type is left to the P4 contract story.

title: The Counts tab is blank and the release column holds values that are not releases
source: 02 Business architecture and process/Recovery Workbench Users Roles and Permissions v4.xlsx
section: Counts tab; Roles tab column 'First release with real users'
description: The Counts tab says it is calculated from the Roles tab, but every cell is blank in v4. Three role classes hold values that are not an E number (No login for PT-LED, Through bank channels for three customer parties, and E4 self-service through bank channels), so a count per release column cannot be computed without a reading rule.
evidence: Counts tab rows 5 to 9: Bank user, Partner user, Customer party, Non-human actor, Total, with every release cell empty; Roles tab values 'No login', 'Through bank channels', 'E4 self-service through bank channels'.
legacy_ref: none (document family, not a legacy story)
proposed: The grid is kept exactly as v4 leaves it; the class totals 37, 7, 4 and 6 that the Roles tab note states are confirmed and restated in the Read me sheet; no per-release count is produced until a reading rule is agreed.

title: The Key tab scope values do not include REGION, which the access story uses
source: 02 Business architecture and process/Recovery Workbench Users Roles and Permissions v4.xlsx; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 037 Role to permission matrix as data and PDPA field masking by role v1.md
section: Key tab Scope rows; Roles tab 'Default scope'; access story BR5 and section 12
description: The Key tab lists four scope values (Own, Team, All, Placed cases). The access story RWB-E1-037 adds REGION to the scope filter and its acceptance criteria use a team and region filter. The two lists disagree and no source says which one is current.
evidence: Key tab rows: Scope Own, Team, All, Placed cases; RWB E1 037 business rule BR5 and section 12 'ScopeFilter type OWN|TEAM|REGION|ALL'.
proposed: The four Key tab values are carried unchanged as the scope of this document; the P4 and P3 design decides whether a region predicate is added and the Key tab is revised only when that decision is taken.

title: No approval and no status is recorded for the document
source: 02 Business architecture and process/Recovery Workbench Users Roles and Permissions v4.xlsx
section: Roles tab note row; Key tab Version row; Read me sheet of v5
description: The workbook carries a version, a date and a supersession note but no status, document owner or approval. Under D-RCV-60 the next version is therefore issued as Draft and the missing approval is recorded rather than waited for.
evidence: Roles tab row 2: 'Version 4, 15 November 2026'; Key tab row 'Version | v4 | 15 November 2026. Supersedes v3'; no status, owner or approval cell in any sheet.
legacy_ref: none (document family, not a legacy story)
proposed: v5 is issued as Draft under D-RCV-60 with the application owner as the approving role; the approval is recorded when the verification loop runs.
